text: Small online sellers lose most of the payment disputes they contest. Often not because they are wrong, but because they missed a deadline, never shared tracking with PayPal, or sent the wrong evidence. Outsourced services take around a quarter of whatever they recover. Rebuttal is an AI dispute co-pilot that works directly with the PayPal Disputes API.

Rebuttal pulls every open dispute from PayPal and matches it to the seller's own order records. The queue is ranked by money at stake against time left, and anything due within a day jumps to the top.

Here is a two hundred and twelve dollar unauthorized transaction chargeback. There is no buyer statement, but Rebuttal read the email history and found that the buyer wrote, got the bowls today, the day after delivery. That quote is verified word for word against the original message.

The win estimate starts from this seller's own history for this dispute reason. Then every PayPal Seller Protection check moves it by a visible amount: delivered to the transaction address, six earlier orders without a dispute, a known device.

{{ENGINE}} drafts the response as sentences that each cite a numbered exhibit. Before anything is sent, a grounding check verifies every date, amount, tracking number and quote against the exhibits it cites.
One click, and Rebuttal submits structured evidence and a PDF exhibit packet to PayPal through the provide evidence endpoint.

Not every dispute is worth fighting. This buyer says one of two mugs arrived chipped. Damage is not covered by Seller Protection, so fighting is worth almost nothing. Rebuttal recommends a twenty eight dollar refund for the broken mug, sent with make offer, along with a friendly message to the buyer.

It is also honest about weak cases. This twelve hundred dollar vase shipped without signature confirmation, so it falls outside Seller Protection. Rebuttal says so, and drops the estimate to thirty four percent.
What if someone edits the response to claim something the evidence does not show? Here I change the delivery date. Rebuttal blocks the submission and points to the exact claim.

Finally, prevention. Rebuttal finds shipped orders whose tracking PayPal never received and pushes them through the Tracking API, so the next item not received claim is covered. It also flags high value orders shipped without a signature.
Rebuttal. Decide which disputes to fight, prove it with grounded evidence, and send it to PayPal in one click. It is open source on GitHub.
